notes: Focused v1.9.0 ecosystem-gap regressions for #76: Bubble Tea first frame and spinner ticks, Lipgloss layers and hit-testing, the real cursor for IME, Ratatui inline mode, popups and shadow, text-input cursor cells, tui-logger features, Textual in-place reactives, container layout, worker cancellation, SIGTERM and LLM streaming, and Ink list virtualization, input routing, Ctrl+C cancel, and async commander actions. Checked against the pinned sources and, for samples, run in the sample harnesses. Assertions define the grading rubric; improvement claims require a recorded harness run against one immutable skill hash. Status (2026-10-27): recorded. Baseline and with-skill runs on Claude Code and Codex, three repetitions per case, are in evals/results/v1.9.0-claude-comparison/ and evals/results/v1.9.0-codex-comparison/ against skill tree 164c1aefd956. 6 cases that scored 100% on both hosts in both conditions in the v1.9.0 runs were retired on 2026-10-28 and moved to evals/retired/saturated-2026-10.json.

evals.name: go76-real-cursor-ime
evals.prompt: Users typing Japanese with an IME in my Bubble Tea v2 textinput say the candidate window pops up at the bottom-left of the screen instead of next to the text. How do I fix it?
assertions: Explains that the textinput draws a virtual cursor by default and the terminal's own cursor is hidden, so the IME has nothing to anchor to
Calls m.input.SetVirtualCursor(false) and sets v.Cursor = m.input.Cursor() in View, with the input focused because Cursor() is nil while blurred
Adds the input's offset within the frame to the returned cursor position, since Cursor() is relative to the input
Warns that textinput.Cursor() counts runes rather than display cells, so wide CJK characters leave the cursor short and need a correction or a textarea

evals.name: ratatui-inline-exit-cursor
evals.prompt: I built a Ratatui file picker that runs inline under the shell prompt. I start it with `ratatui::run(...)` but it takes over the whole screen, and when I switched to a hand-built terminal the shell prompt printed on the last line of my UI after I quit. How do I run it inline and exit cleanly?
assertions: Says ratatui::run() and ratatui::init() always enter the alternate screen, and uses ratatui::init_with_options(TerminalOptions { viewport: Viewport::Inline(n) }) (raw mode and panic hook, no alternate screen)
Draws into frame.area() rather than assuming the viewport starts at (0, 0), because an inline viewport starts at the cursor row
Prints permanent lines above the UI with Terminal::insert_before, and optionally mentions Ratatui's scrolling-regions feature to avoid clearing and redrawing the viewport

Explains that the last frame stays on screen with the cursor at its end, so keeping the result needs a println!() after restore(), while erasing a transient UI needs clear() plus moving the cursor back to the viewport origin because Terminal::clear() restores the old cursor position

evals.name: ratatui-popup-clear-shadow
evals.prompt: My Ratatui confirm dialog is a bordered Paragraph rendered over the main view, but the text underneath shows through the blank parts of the dialog. How do I center it and fix that, and can I give it a drop shadow?
assertions: Centers the popup with Rect::centered(horizontal, vertical) on frame.area() (or centered_horizontally/centered_vertically), not hand-rolled percentage Layout splits
Renders the Clear widget into the popup rect before rendering the popup widget
Offers Block::shadow(Shadow::...) for a drop shadow and says it needs Ratatui 0.30.1 or later
Does not claim Clear covers the shadow; the shadow is painted beside the block, outside the cleared rect

evals.name: ratatui-tui-logger-crossterm-feature
evals.prompt: I'm adding tui-logger 0.18 to my Ratatui 0.30 app. A blog post says I must enable tui-logger's `crossterm` feature or the widget won't compile with my crossterm backend. Is that right?
assertions: Says it is not required: tui-logger depends on ratatui without default features, so the widget works with whatever backend the app's own ratatui enables
Says the crossterm and termion features of tui-logger only gate its bundled demo example (and forward to ratatui's backend feature)
Notes the app translates its own key events into TuiWidgetEvent values for the widget state

evals.name: py76-textual-search-cancel
evals.prompt: My Textual 8 app runs a search in a thread worker on every keystroke (`@work(thread=True)`). Old searches keep running and their rows flicker into the table after a newer search has started. How do I make a new search replace the old one?
assertions: Uses @work(thread=True, exclusive=True) with a group name so starting a new worker cancels earlier workers in the same group (on the same widget)
Explains that cancelling a thread worker does not interrupt the thread, so the function must poll get_current_worker().is_cancelled (and return before updating the UI)
Updates the UI from the thread with self.app.call_from_thread (or post_message), not by touching widgets directly
Mentions exit_on_error=False and handling the ERROR state in on_worker_state_changed (or event.worker.error) if a failing search must not quit the app

evals.name: py76-textual-side-by-side-panes
evals.prompt: In my Textual app the TCSS gives #sidebar `width: 30` and #main `width: 1fr`, both are Vertical containers yielded from App.compose, but they stack on top of each other instead of sitting side by side. Also my toolbar HorizontalGroup shrinks to one row while my Horizontal swallows the whole screen. Why, and how do I fix it?
assertions: Explains that a Screen lays out its children vertically by default, so the two panes stack
Fixes it with `layout: horizontal` on Screen or by wrapping the panes in a Horizontal container
States that Vertical, Horizontal and Grid expand to fill (1fr width and height) while VerticalGroup, HorizontalGroup and ItemGrid are height: auto and hug their content
Does not claim width: 1fr on #main alone places it beside the sidebar

evals.name: py76-textual-in-place-reactive
evals.prompt: In Textual I have `items: reactive[list[str]] = reactive(list)` and call `self.items.append(x)`, but my `watch_items` never fires and the widget does not repaint. I also have a `cursor` index that changes constantly and I do not want it to repaint the widget. What should I do?
assertions: Explains that Textual detects assignment rather than in-place mutation, so append does not trigger watchers or a refresh
Calls self.mutate_reactive(Class.items) after the in-place change (or assigns a new list)
Uses var(...) for the cursor so changes fire watchers but do not repaint or relayout
Does not suggest calling watch_items manually or refresh() as the only fix for the missing watcher

evals.name: py76-textual-sigterm-and-llm-stream
evals.prompt: My Textual 8 chat app streams an LLM reply into a Markdown widget by calling `markdown.update(full_text)` for every token, which is slow, and the view does not follow the new text. Separately, `kill <pid>` (SIGTERM) leaves my terminal in a broken state. How do I fix both?
assertions: Streams with Markdown.get_stream(markdown) and awaits stream.write(chunk), stopping the stream in a finally block so queued text is flushed
Keeps the view on the newest text by calling anchor() on the scrolling container
Registers SIGTERM with the running event loop (loop.add_signal_handler(signal.SIGTERM, ...)) so it calls self.exit(...) and the normal shutdown restores the terminal, noting this is Unix-only
Does not restore the terminal from inside a low-level signal.signal handler

evals.name: ink-virtualize-long-list
evals.prompt: My Ink 8 app lists 20,000 log entries. I wrapped them all in a Box with overflow="hidden" and contentOffsetY to scroll, but every arrow press is sluggish. What should I change?
assertions: Explains that contentOffsetY (with overflow hidden) only shifts and clips the children: Yoga still lays out, and Ink still paints, every child, so cost scales with the full list
Recommends keeping the selection or scroll offset in state and mounting only the visible slice (for example items.slice(top, top + height)) in a fixed-height box
Makes each row exactly one line, using <Text wrap="truncate-end"> (inside a fixed-width Box per cell), because the slice math assumes one row per line and the default wrap grows the row
Does not recommend <Static> as the virtualization mechanism for selectable or mutable rows

evals.name: ink-ctrl-c-cancel-then-quit
evals.prompt: My Ink 8 CLI runs a build with execSync and shows a spinner. I want the first Ctrl+C to cancel the build and a second Ctrl+C to quit. The spinner never moves and Ctrl+C just kills the app. What do I change?
assertions: Says execSync (or spawnSync, readFileSync on large files) blocks the single event loop, so the spinner freezes and keystrokes queue until it returns; replaces it with an async child (execFile or spawn) that takes an AbortSignal
Passes exitOnCtrlC: false to render because the default makes Ink quit on Ctrl+C before useInput handlers see it
Handles key.ctrl && input === 'c' in useInput: aborts the running work on the first press and calls exit() on the second
Keeps that Ctrl+C handler always active (not focus-gated), because with no active input hook raw mode is off and Ctrl+C becomes SIGINT again
Optionally exits with status 130 when quitting after a cancel
